map.MAP 平均动脉压 使用指南: MAP Mean Arterial Pressure User Guide
map.MAP 平均动脉压计算器。输入收缩压与舒张压，按 MAP ≈ 舒张压 + (收缩: MAP mean arterial pressure calculator. Enter systolic and diastolic pressure and estimate MAP as MAP ≈ diastolic + (systolic − diastolic)/3; it reflects organ perfusion pressure and is used as a reference for circulation monitoring.
map.器官灌注：MAP 反映心脑肾等平均灌注压: Organ perfusion: MAP reflects average perfusion pressure to heart, brain and kidneys
map.休克监测：MAP<65 常需升压维持灌注: Shock monitoring: MAP below 65 usually needs vasopressors to maintain perfusion
map.血压管理：结合收缩压/舒张压看整体: Blood pressure management: read systolic and diastolic together for the whole picture
map.：算法：MAP ≈ 舒张压 + (收缩压−舒张压)/3；脉压 = 收缩压−舒张压: : algorithm: MAP ≈ diastolic pressure + (systolic − diastolic)/3; pulse pressure = systolic − diastolic; grading: MAP at least 70 normal, 65-69 borderline, below 65 low. Blood pressure must be greater than 0.
map.：例1（120/80）：MAP=80+(120−80)/3=93.3mmHg，脉: : example 1 (120/80): MAP = 80 + (120 − 80)/3 = 93.3 mmHg, pulse pressure 40 mmHg, normal. Example 2 (100/60): MAP = 73.3 mmHg, normal. Example 3 (90/55): MAP = 66.7 mmHg, borderline.
map.医疗健康类结果为按公式得到的估算值，不能替代医生诊断与处方。给药剂量、补液速度、: Medical and health results are estimates from formulas and cannot replace a doctor's diagnosis or prescription. Dosage, infusion rate, anticoagulation and thrombolysis decisions must follow the drug label, clinical guidelines and the attending physician; for emergencies such as chest pain, difficulty breathing or altered consciousness seek care immediately.
map.MAP 比收缩压重要吗？: Is MAP more important than systolic pressure?
map.MAP 更代表器官平均灌注，尤其麻醉/ICU 关注 MAP 是否≥65；但收缩压: MAP better represents average organ perfusion, and anesthesia/ICU care particularly watches whether MAP is at least 65; but very low systolic pressure also affects coronary perfusion, so judge both together.
map.舒张期占整个心动周期约 2/3，故权重 2/3 给舒张压、1/3 给脉压，即 D: Diastole occupies about 2/3 of the cardiac cycle, so weight 2/3 goes to diastolic pressure and 1/3 to pulse pressure, i.e. DBP + PP/3, an empirical approximation.
